solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pre-owned Subaru sedan parts

indicators.note: parts says a piece of the two words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A second-hand dealer selling components from a Subaru saloon car.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had a previous owner, so pre-owned is the dealer's euphemism for that.

clue.text: Narcoleptic's breakfast?

parts.note: a narcoleptic nods off constantly, so is one who naps; that word is also a smoked herring eaten at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: To kip is British slang for to sleep, so a person who sleeps would be one who kips; the word is also a split smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: The smoked fish is a breakfast staple, while the sleepy reading makes it a person who naps.

clue.text: Rogue Serge ultimately charmed 'BB' into boudoir

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward, so the letters go astray and are reordered
ultimately points to the final letter of Serge

explanation.surface: The rakish singer Serge Gainsbourg seduces Brigitte Bardot, known as BB, into a lady's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, which joins CHARMED and BB for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a woman's private room, traditionally a sleeping chamber, an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Drawn painstakingly and rumoured to be of value

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so a spoken form is wanted

parts.note: something prized is held to be of value

explanation.surface: A portrait drawn with great care is said to be worth something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like sketching; it is pulled out with effort, as a lid is levered off.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise is to lever or force something out with difficulty, so it was drawn out painstakingly.

clue.text: Idiot Delia got up and attacked

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the name Delia is written upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A foolish Delia rose to her feet and launched an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses DELIA to AILED, as the clue runs down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, so the past tense matches attacked exactly.

clue.text: This bends the definition: born within the boundaries of Knightsbridge

indicators.note: within puts the born letters inside the boundary letters
boundaries are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Knightsbridge

parts.note: NE comes from French né, meaning born

explanation.surface: A quirky statement that being born inside Knightsbridge stretches the definition of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'This bends' is the definition, 'the definition:' announces it. Knightsbridge is a wealthy London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint is the part of the body that bends, so it is described by its action.

clue.text: Suggestion winding-up will split union in confusion

indicators.note: a thing that will split another goes into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other
in confusion means the letters of union are jumbled

parts.note: a winding-up is an end

explanation.surface: A company liquidation will divide a muddled trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding-up' looks like a company liquidation; here it simply means a finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation or indirect hint, often suggestive, is an oblique suggestion.

clue.text: On-air journalist's 'Wanderers' broadcast covering East

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, so the definition reads on-air journalist

indicators.note: covering means the jumbled letters wrap round the compass letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A radio journalist reports on Wanderers, a football team, covering the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton or Wolves are 'Wanderers' football clubs. 'broadcast' scrambles WANDERERS; 'covering' wraps the result round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter who reads the bulletin on radio or television is an on-air journalist.

clue.text: Confectionery spat out in train

indicators.note: words spat out are spoken, so the clue wants a word said aloud rather than written

parts.note: a sweet is a piece of confectionery

explanation.surface: Someone spits out a mouthful of sweets while travelling on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway, but it is a retinue; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue of attendants following a dignitary, as a royal train does, is also called a suite.

clue.text: Effect of 'Good Vibrations' succeeded in an encore being ruined

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the words an encore are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A band's encore of the Beach Boys hit 'Good Vibrations' falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being ruined' turns AN ENCORE into REONANCE, and 'in' places S after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Good vibrations reverberate, and that sustained reverberating sound is the physical effect named here.

clue.text: Heads of Counter Intelligence returning in 'Department S' shows

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pair inside the other letters

parts.note: DEPTS is departments abbreviated; Department S was a 1960s British TV spy series

indicators.note: returning means the two initials are read backwards
heads of takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A spy-drama plot: counter-intelligence chiefs come back in an episode of the TV series Department S.
explanation.walkthrough: Department S was a 1969 British TV thriller series; here it supplies the abbreviation for departments.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to portray or represent, so it is a synonym of shows as a verb.

clue.text: Society after a site offering means of access

indicators.note: after says the society letter comes at the end, behind the rest

parts.note: a venue is a site where an event is held

explanation.surface: A club looks for a location that offers good access.
explanation.definitionFit: Approach roads, and figuratively possible routes to a goal, are ways in, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Yashmak rubbernecker repelled, making a case for public cover-up?

indicators.note: repelled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words make a case, a container, holding the wanted letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A veiled woman drives off a gawping onlooker, a good argument for covering up in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'making a case for' into the definition, leaving the concealment with no indicator; it is the signal that the two words enclose the letters, so the definition is just 'public cover-up?'.
explanation.definitionFit: This full-body garment worn by some Muslim women covers the wearer completely whenever she is out in public.

clue.text: Cherub model or minder?

parts.note: a cherub is a chubby infant, a baby
an artist's model is a sitter

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is a cherubic model or a carer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after a child while the parents are out is a minder of that child.

clue.text: Industry verges on inching into terrible decline

indicators.note: into puts the edge letters inside the rearranged word
terrible says the word decline is in a terrible mess, so its letters are reordered
verges are edges, so the first and last letters of inching are taken

explanation.surface: A report of a nation's industry edging towards awful decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Industry' looks like the economy in the surface; it is the definition in its sense of hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in the sense of hard-working application is a synonym of steady careful effort.

clue.text: Scotsman in sports car sees unruly small and big girls

indicators.note: in places the Scotsman inside the car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a sports car badge
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of sees are disorderly, rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A Scot in a sports car spots some small and large girls behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns SEES into ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Female giants are huge women, so big girls fits them literally.

clue.text: Babe Ruth, say, or where he shone

definitions.meaning: the great American hitter was a jewel of his sport, a gem of that game
the infield on which he played and starred

explanation.surface: A tribute to the American baseball legend Babe Ruth and the ground where he starred.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the most famous US baseball player of the 1920s; the first reading treats him as a precious stone of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a star player as a gem of his sport; the other is the square playing field of the game.

clue.text: In court this could be an advantage

definitions.text: In court this could be an advantage

parts.words: In court this could be an advantage
parts.note: on a tennis court, a player with advantage may be one rally from winning a set, the tennis sense rather than the legal one

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, where advantage is the score after deuce.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the score at which one rally would win the set is this, and it may come at advantage.

clue.text: Drawing charmed one employed by Fagin?

parts.note: a charmed life is a lucky one
Fagin in Oliver Twist ran a gang of pickpockets, and a dip is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: Someone with a charmed life is recruited into Fagin's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: A lucky dip is a British fairground game where prizes are drawn blind from a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a random draw of a prize from a container, so it is a kind of drawing.

clue.text: It's racial in the guise of irreverent

indicators.note: in the guise of says the letters appear disguised, in a different form

explanation.surface: A complaint that something racial is passed off as merely irreverent humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, scornful humour that targets the powerful is irreverent in spirit, a close synonym.

clue.text: Relax — there's old and new entering winter sport separately

indicators.note: entering puts the two letters inside the sport
separately says the two letters go in at different places

parts.note: the luge is a winter sport of sledging feet-first

explanation.surface: An instruction to unwind: old and new competitors join a sledging event at different times.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes in after the L and N after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to recline lazily and take it easy, a synonym of unwinding.

clue.text: Friend without question following termination of contract is acquisitive type

indicators.note: following says the trimmed Friend comes after the contract's final letter
the termination of a word is its final letter
without says the question letters are removed

parts.note: a Friend is a member of the Society of Friends, the Quakers

explanation.surface: A friend who stops asking questions once a deal ends turns out to be grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: Friend with a capital is a member of the Religious Society of Friends, a Quaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually grabs and accepts whatever is offered is an acquisitive type.

clue.text: Warden who shows potential for long-term relationship?

definitions.meaning: a warden is a custodian, as of a park or a museum

definitions.text: who shows potential for long-term relationship?
definitions.meaning: a partner worth holding on to, in the dating idiom

explanation.surface: A prison warden who seems promising as a long-term partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a guardian; a partner worth holding on to is, in the dating idiom, one to keep.

clue.text: Dolly with her head in the clouds may be behind this

definitions.meaning: a dolly is a wheeled platform, as used for moving a film camera

definitions.text: with her head in the clouds may be behind this
definitions.meaning: a dreamy, dotty woman is said to be off her rocker, here off this wheeled cart

explanation.surface: A girl called Dolly, a daydreamer, gets blamed for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly looks like a name; it is a wheeled cart. The second reading alludes to the idiom off one's trolley, meaning crazy, so a dotty person has left it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wheeled cart for moving loads or a camera is a dolly; the British idiom off one's trolley means mad.

clue.text: Globetrotter spilling gin-and-tonic — bounder! — where studs hang out

indicators.note: spilling means losing letters, so the drink and the cad are taken out

parts.note: the remaining letters also sit in a row inside this word, a coincidence of the deletion: the clue removes the drink and the cad
a G and T is a gin and tonic
a rotter is a cad, a bounder

explanation.surface: A world traveller, a cad, spills a G and T in a bar where studly men gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G and T and ROTTER from GLOBETROTTER leaves four letters. 'studs' looks like macho men; they are earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud earrings are worn through the soft fleshy lower part of the ear.

clue.text: Quiffed couriers were in tears

parts.note: UPS is a well-known parcel courier company
to weep is to cry, so were in tears means wept

explanation.surface: The delivery drivers cried over their elaborate hairstyles.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiff is hair brushed up and back from the forehead, so a quiffed style has its hair swept upward.

clue.text: The point of some pachyderms

parts.note: elephants and walruses have long pointed ivory teeth, the sharp point of the animal

explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like purpose, as in what is the point; it is a literal sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long protruding ivory tooth ends in a sharp point.

clue.text: Fashion neon jewellery — it can be dignifying

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters of neon are rearranged

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Bright neon-coloured jewellery is said, surprisingly, to lend its wearer dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage or conferring honour gives them dignity and nobility, so it is dignifying.

clue.text: Quits during elevenses?

indicators.note: during says the letters sit within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their job during the mid-morning tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is the British mid-morning snack break. 'Quits' looks like a verb; it is the adjective meaning square.
explanation.definitionFit: When debts are settled and neither owes the other, the parties are square, all level.
